t: A German princess with no claim to the Russian throne, Catherine took it in 1762 by a coup against her husband Peter III, who died eight days later in unexplained circumstances.

In a reign of over 34 years she extended the empire by some 520,000 square kilometres at the expense mainly of the Ottoman Empire and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, and reorganised provincial government, education and Church property.
She brought the abolition of serfdom into public debate, but the exploitation of serf labour intensified under her and was one of the chief reasons behind Pugachev's Rebellion.
dyk: To promote smallpox inoculation, then a controversial method, Catherine had herself inoculated in 1768 by the English doctor Thomas Dimsdale; by 1800 approximately 2 million inoculations had been administered in the Russian Empire.
ev: Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst, the future Catherine, is born in Stettin, where her father is governor
Having been received into the Orthodox Church as Catherine the year before, she marries the heir to the Russian throne, the future Peter III
With the support of guards regiments she overthrows Peter III six months after his accession and begins her reign as Catherine II
She secularises the lands of the Russian Orthodox Church and has her former lover Stanislaus Augustus Poniatowski placed on the Polish throne
The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca ends a victorious war with the Ottoman Empire; Pugachev's Rebellion spreads among serfs and peasants
Catherine annexes Crimea, and Georgia becomes a Russian protectorate by the Treaty of Georgievsk
Russia, Prussia and Austria divide the remaining territory of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in the third partition
Catherine suffers a stroke and dies the following evening; her son succeeds as Paul I

f.born: 2 May 1729 in Stettin (now Szczecin), Pomerania, Kingdom of Prussia, as Princess Sophie Auguste Friederike von Anhalt-Zerbst; daughter of Christian August, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, and Joanna Elisabeth of Holstein-Gottorp
f.died: 17 November 1796, the evening after a stroke that left her in a coma; an autopsy confirmed the stroke as the cause
f.role: Grand duchess as wife of the heir Peter (from 1745); empress consort (1762); Empress of Russia from 9 July 1762 until her death in 1796
f.known: the coup of 1762 against Peter III; wars with the Ottoman Empire and the annexation of Crimea in 1783; the partitions of Poland; the provincial reform of 1775 and the charters of 1785; the secularisation of Church lands; the Smolny Institute and a state school system; the Hermitage; her correspondence with Voltaire
